transcript.content: Hi, I’m glad you came in today. What brings you in?

Hi, doctor. Thank you so much for fitting me in. I really appreciate it, and I hope I'm not taking up too much of your time. 

I'm just here because... well, it's probably just normal stress, right? Being a supervisor at the store, there's always a lot to juggle. But lately, when I try to explain things to my team—like the inventory numbers or the weekend schedule—I... I guess my words just sort of start jumping around a bit. I'll be talking about the delivery trucks, and then somehow I'm on about Thursdays, and then the church grill, and then my boss’s tone of voice. 

People just look at me like... like they can’t follow what I’m saying at all. It's a little embarrassing, honestly, because I really do try to be a good manager. I'm trying my best to communicate clearly, but... does that make sense? I just want to make sure I'm explaining this okay for you.
Have you been feeling unusually energetic lately, like you need much less sleep than usual?

Oh, no, doctor. I don't... I don't think so. I always try to make sure I get a good night's rest, you know? I really want to make sure I'm sharp for the team the next day, so I wouldn't say I'm unusually energetic or anything like that. 

Honestly, keeping up with the store floor at my age takes a fair bit out of you, so I definitely still need my sleep. I've just been sleeping my normal amount. I hope that's okay? I mean, I hope I'm giving you the right kind of information for what you're looking for. I just haven't noticed any changes with my energy like that.
Have you been hearing voices when no one else is around?

Voices? Oh, um... no, doctor. No, I wouldn't say that. I mean, sometimes when the store is really quiet, I might think I hear someone calling from the stockroom, but that's just normal, right? Just the building settling, or maybe the hum of the refrigerators. 

I definitely don't hear anything... unusual or anything that isn't there. I know how important it is to be clear about these things, and I wouldn't want you to think I'm... well, that I'm losing my grip or anything. I'm just a bit stressed, like I said. Does that sound like a normal thing to you? I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right answers.
Have you started to believe that someone is trying to harm you or plot against you?

Oh, goodness, no. No, doctor. I don't think anyone is plotting against me. I mean, retail can be competitive, and sometimes the corporate office makes decisions that feel a bit out of touch, but... no, I certainly don't think anyone is actually trying to harm me. 

I've always tried to be a good colleague and treat everyone with respect, so I'd like to think I haven't made any enemies. It's just the stress of the job, like I mentioned. I really hope I'm not giving the impression that I'm paranoid or anything like that. I'm just a regular guy trying to do my best at work. That's a good thing, right? I just want to make sure I'm answering your questions the way you need me to.
Did this trouble with your words start very suddenly?

Suddenly? Oh, um... well, no, doctor, I wouldn't say it was sudden. I always try to be very clear when I'm directing the team, but... I guess, if I'm being completely honest, it's been going on for a little while. Maybe... about six months now? 

I've just had these little moments on the sales floor where my explanations get a bit, you know, jumbled. And sometimes I just sort of... make these odd stops when I'm talking or walking the floor. It's just a little embarrassing, to be truthful. I always try to play it off so the staff and the customers don't think poorly of me or think I'm not up to the job anymore. 

Does six months sound like a normal timeline for someone who's just dealing with a lot of pressure? I really hope I'm explaining this the way you need me to. I just want to be as helpful as I can.
During these past six months, have you had a period of at least two weeks when you felt depressed most of the day nearly every day?

Depressed? Oh, um... no, doctor. I really wouldn't say that. I mean, sure, everyone gets a little tired or worn out sometimes, especially after a long week on the sales floor, but... no, definitely not sad or depressed for two weeks straight. 

I always try to keep a positive attitude for the team. You kind of have to, right? If the supervisor looks down, it brings the whole store's morale down. So I make it a point to stay upbeat and keep things moving. I haven't felt anything like what you're describing, not all day like that. 

That's a good sign, isn't it? I just want to make sure I'm doing okay and answering everything the way you need me to.
Have you started believing things that other people say are not true, even though they feel completely real to you?

Believing things that aren't true? Oh, um... no. No, doctor, definitely not. I've always prided myself on being a very practical person. You sort of have to be when you're managing a store, right? You deal with inventory and schedules and real, tangible things every day. 

So, no, I haven't had any... unusual beliefs or anything like that. If someone tells me I've got something wrong, I'm usually pretty good at stepping back and seeing their side of it. I just try to focus on the facts and keep my feet on the ground. 

I hope that's a good thing? I really want to make sure I'm giving you the right information. I'm trying my best to be helpful... am I answering these the way you need me to?
During the time your speech has been getting jumbled, have you had times when you felt unusually happy or high?

Unusually happy or high? Oh, um... no, doctor. I wouldn't say that at all. I mean, I like to think I'm a fairly even-keeled person. I get a little satisfaction when we hit our sales targets for the week, or when a customer leaves a nice review about the team, but... just normal happiness, you know? 

I certainly haven't felt anything extreme or... or out of control. I try to keep a very steady demeanor. It's important to be reliable when you're the supervisor, so I make sure I'm always level-headed for the staff. 

So, no, nothing like being unusually high or anything. I hope that's the kind of answer you're looking for? I just want to make sure I'm giving you a clear picture of how I've been doing. Am I doing okay with these questions?
Over the past several months, have you found yourself losing interest in things you used to care about?

Losing interest? Oh, well... no, I wouldn't say I've lost interest in things. I mean, I still go to work every day, and I still care very much about the store and the team. 

I suppose... well, maybe I don't go out quite as much on the weekends as I used to, but that's just because I'm getting older, right? I'm 59 now, so I think it's perfectly normal to want to just stay in and rest after a busy week on the floor. It's not that I don't care about my hobbies or anything, I just... I prioritize my energy for work. I always want to make sure I'm giving my best to the staff. 

So, I wouldn't call it losing interest, just being a bit more responsible with my time. That makes sense, doesn't it? I hope I'm explaining that clearly enough for you, doctor. I really want to be helpful.
Have you felt that outside forces are putting thoughts into your mind that are not your own?

Thoughts being put into my mind? Oh, my. No, doctor, definitely not. That sounds... well, that sounds very frightening, to be honest. 

I've always been very clear on what I'm thinking. I mean, as a supervisor, you have to be decisive, right? You have to know your own mind to make schedules and handle customer complaints. I wouldn't be able to do my job if I felt like someone else was... putting things in my head. 

Sometimes, I suppose, if I'm really tired after a long shift, I might get a song stuck in my head, or keep replaying a conversation with a difficult customer, but that's just normal stress, isn't it? That's just my own brain trying to process the day. 

I certainly don't feel like any outside forces are involved. I'm very much in control of my own thoughts. I hope that's the right answer? I mean, I hope that shows I'm doing okay. I'm really trying to be as cooperative as possible with all these questions.
Have other people told you that your face or voice seems less expressive than it used to?

Less expressive? Oh, um... no, I don't think anyone has said anything like that to me. I try to be very polite and professional with everyone, especially at the store. 

I mean, maybe sometimes I don't smile quite as big by the end of a long shift, but that's just because my feet hurt, you know? It's not that I'm not expressing myself, I'm just focusing on getting the closing duties done so everyone can go home. I always make sure to greet the customers warmly when they come in, though. 

I really try to be a pleasant person to be around. I hope I'm coming across that way to you, too? I certainly don't want anyone to think I'm being cold or... or unapproachable. I'm doing my best to be helpful and engaged here, doctor. Is that alright?
Have you felt that other people can hear or know your thoughts, even when you haven’t said them out loud?

People hearing my thoughts? Oh, goodness, no. No, doctor, I've never felt anything like that. 

I mean... sometimes at the store, my assistant manager will hand me the break schedule before I even ask for it, but that's just because we've worked together for so long, right? She just knows my routine and anticipates what I need. It's certainly not because she's actually reading my mind or hearing what I'm thinking. 

I keep my private thoughts very much to myself. I'd really hate to think someone could just... listen in on me. That would be quite inappropriate, wouldn't it? I assure you, my thoughts are completely private. I hope that's a normal answer? I just want to make sure I'm giving you exactly what you need for your notes, doctor. I'm trying my very best to be helpful.
Have there been times when your body feels stuck, like you freeze and cannot move or respond for a while?

Stuck? Like, freezing up completely? Oh, no, doctor, I wouldn't say I get stuck or frozen. I'm always moving, always trying to keep busy. 

I mean... I suppose there are times when I might get a little... distracted? Or maybe just very focused on a particular task. Like, sometimes on the sales floor, I'll catch myself pacing the same aisle, you know, straightening the exact same row of batteries over and over. Or... well, sometimes I'll just be standing there with the schedule clipboard in my hand, and I guess I lose track of time for a minute, and the associates are just kind of waiting for me to tell them what to do. 

But I'm not frozen! I'm just... I'm just thinking really hard about how to organize the shift, or making sure the display looks absolutely perfect. As a supervisor, you really want things to be orderly, right? It's just me trying to be thorough and do a good job. I hope that makes sense? I'm sure everyone gets a little lost in thought sometimes when they're working hard, don't they? I really want to assure you I'm still doing my job.
When you stand there with the clipboard, do other people find that you do not respond when they speak to you?

Oh, no... no, I definitely answer them. I would never just ignore my team. That would be a pretty terrible way to manage people, wouldn't it? 

I mean, maybe... maybe sometimes the store music is a bit loud, or I'm just so focused on the payroll numbers that I don't catch what they say on the very first try. But I always respond. I might just say, "Give me one second," while I finish my thought, but I always get right back to them. 

I really pride myself on being accessible and supportive to my associates. I hope that sounds like a normal work environment to you? I certainly wouldn't want you to think I'm just... tuning people out or neglecting my duties. I try very hard to be a good listener for them.
Have you ever felt that ordinary things around you—like the TV, radio, or signs in the store—were sending you special messages meant just for you?

Special messages? Oh, my, no. No, doctor, I've never experienced anything like that. 

I mean... the signs in the store, they're just the standard promotional materials corporate sends down every week. You know, 'Buy One Get One' or the seasonal endcap displays. I just make sure my team hangs them up straight and they look nice for the customers. There's certainly no... secret meaning to them. They just are what they are. 

And the TV or the radio, well, I just listen to the traffic report on the commute, or maybe watch a little bit of the evening news when I get home to unwind. It's all just regular, everyday information. I wouldn't even know what a special message would look like, to be perfectly honest. 

I try to keep my feet firmly on the ground, doctor. That’s a good thing, right? I hope that shows I’m doing well. I just want to be completely open with you so you can see that I’m cooperating and trying to be a good patient.
Have other people told you that your behavior seems strange or disorganized?

Strange? Oh, no... well, I wouldn't use a word like *strange*. I think sometimes people just have different ways of doing things, and maybe my way is just a little... unique right now? 

I mean, I suppose there have been a few little adjustments at work. My manager, he... well, he decided to take me off the busy weekend shifts. But I think that's just because weekends are so chaotic, and he knows I like things to be very orderly and precise. He did mention in my last performance review that we need to see some improvements, or... or there could be a suspension. But I'm sure he just wants me to be the best supervisor I can be! I'm working really hard to show him I can handle it. That's the right attitude to have, isn't it?

And at home... well, my wife is just so wonderful and supportive. She's been taking on a few more of the things I usually handle, like some of our social commitments or talking to the neighbors. She said some people were getting a little... well, maybe just a bit confused by how focused or intense I can get sometimes. But she just wants to help me relax. It's perfectly normal for spouses to help each other out when one is under a little stress, right? I really hope you can see that I'm trying my absolute best to keep everything running smoothly.
Have you felt that someone is controlling your actions or movements?

Oh, no. No, certainly not. I'm... I'm completely in control of myself, doctor. 

I mean, I make my own decisions every day. I decide when to get up, how to set the floor displays at work, what to have for dinner... it's all just me. I wouldn't even know how someone could control my movements. That sounds like something out of a science fiction movie, doesn't it? 

I always take full responsibility for my actions, both at the store and at home. I think accountability is so important, especially for a supervisor. You have to be the one steering the ship, so to speak. I hope that's the kind of answer you're looking for? I really want to assure you that I'm fully present and in charge of my own behavior.
Have you felt that people are watching you or talking about you behind your back?

Oh, goodness, no. I don't think so. 

I mean... working in retail, you always have people looking your way, but that's just customers needing help finding something on the floor, or checking to see if a register is open. It's just a normal part of the job. 

And as for my team... well, I try to be a very fair supervisor. I suppose they might grumble a little bit about the holiday schedule now and then, but that's just standard workplace chatter, isn't it? I always make it a point to treat everyone with respect, so I don't think anyone would have any reason to whisper about me or plot behind my back. 

I just try to keep a very positive attitude and get along with everyone. That’s the best way to handle things, don't you think? I really hope that shows I'm maintaining good, healthy relationships with the people around me. I always try to be a team player.
Have you ever stayed in one position for a long time, even when it became uncomfortable, without moving much?

Oh, well... stay in one position? Like, completely frozen? No, no, I wouldn't say I do that. That sounds... well, that sounds like something to be worried about, doesn't it? I'm always moving, always trying to be productive. 

Though... I suppose there are moments at the store where I might... get a little caught up in the details. You know how important presentation is in retail. Sometimes I'll catch myself pacing the exact same aisle, just back and forth, making sure every single row of batteries is perfectly straight. Over and over. Just... making sure it's right. 

And, well, there have been a couple of times where I've just been standing there with the schedule clipboard in my hand... just sort of pausing for a moment, while the associates are waiting for me to give them their tasks. I guess it might look like I'm stuck, but I'm really just... thinking very deeply about the best way to organize the shift. It's so important to be thorough, right? I just want to make sure I'm doing a good job for the team. That's a good quality for a supervisor to have, being detail-oriented, isn't it?
Has anyone told you that you repeat the same movements or tasks over and over, even when there is no need to?

Oh... well, I suppose I did sort of just mention that, didn't I? Um... yes, a few people at the store have... pointed it out. Very politely, of course! They're a wonderful team, very respectful. 

Like I was saying, one of the cashiers did ask me the other day why I was pacing that same aisle, straightening the exact same row of batteries over and over again. I think they were just curious, really. And... well, yes, when I'm just standing there with the schedule clipboard in my hand, sometimes the associates will sort of... gently clear their throats or ask me if I'm ready, because they've been waiting a little while for me to tell them what to do. 

I always just tell them I'm double-checking the plan. I really don't want you to think I'm neglecting my duties or just wasting time on the clock. I just get very focused on making sure the store looks its absolute best, and that everyone is assigned to the right department. That's just being a dedicated employee, don't you think? I really try my best to be thorough, and I hope that shows I care about my job.
